About MAPAC

The Muslim American Political Action Committee (MAPAC) is a 501(c)(4) nonprofit organization built by and for Muslim Americans. That status matters, and it's worth explaining plainly.

A 501(c)(4) is a mission-driven nonprofit — not a super PAC. Super PACs exist to pour unlimited money into elections. MAPAC is the opposite of that: we are people-powered, funded by our members and supporters, and our primary work is serving our community's welfare — educating voters, speaking to power, and standing up for justice. We don't buy elections. We organize people.

What we do

Civic and political engagement. As a social-welfare organization, we can and do advocate directly for our community — meeting with elected officials, speaking out on legislation, registering voters, hosting candidate forums, and publishing voter guides. When candidates earn our trust through their record, we endorse them; when they don't, we say so. Holding power accountable is part of our mission, not a side project.

Media and public voice. We work with journalists and media outlets to present honest perspectives on issues affecting Muslims, to answer misinformation, and to make sure a Muslim voice is part of the story. Our long-running program MAPAC-Live TV has brought Muslim and non-Muslim guests together for open conversation on local, national, and international issues.

Our roots

MAPAC is a registered political action committee — filed with the Federal Election Commission and the Commonwealth of Virginia. That registration is a public promise: our finances are a matter of public record, our endorsements are made in the open, and we are accountable to the law and to the community we serve.

We were founded in 2002, in the years after September 11, when Muslim Americans faced a wave of suspicion and backlash. Our founders believed the answer was not to retreat, but to participate — to build real relationships with elected officials, to register voters, and to make sure our community shows up, every election.

That belief still guides everything we do. Today, as a registered PAC, we put it into practice the way the law intends: evaluating candidates on their record, endorsing those who earn it, supporting them within the limits of the law, and holding them accountable after Election Day.

Why it matters

Across America, communities have built political homes for themselves. The Latino Victory Fund grows Latino political power. The AAPI Victory Fund mobilizes Asian American and Pacific Islander voters. The Collective PAC works for Black representation at every level of government. Emgage organizes Muslim American voters in key states.

MAPAC is part of that same American tradition: ordinary people organizing to be heard. When our community votes, candidates listen. When candidates listen, policies change — on civil rights, on war and peace, on the dignity of every human being.

Our promise

We are independent. We answer to our community and our mission — not to big donors, not to special interests, and not to any party. We endorse candidates who earn it through their words, their votes, and their courage.

Vote your conscience. Demand justice. Hold power accountable.

Candidate research

Contribution rules

By contributing to MAPAC, you confirm that:

  • This contribution is made from your own funds, and the funds are not being provided to you by another person or entity for the purpose of making this contribution.
  • You are at least 18 years old.
  • You are a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted permanent resident (green card holder).
  • You are not a federal contractor.
  • This contribution is not from a corporation, labor organization, or foreign national.

Limits and reporting

An individual may contribute up to $5,000 per calendar year to MAPAC. Contributions totaling more than $200 in a calendar year are itemized in MAPAC's public FEC reports (name, address, occupation, and employer). MAPAC's finances are a matter of public record.

Contributions to MAPAC are not tax-deductible as charitable contributions for federal income tax purposes.
